question: Pipe P can fill (3)/(8) part of a tank in 21 hours and pipe Q can fill (2)/(7) part of the same tank in 16 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 2 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 3 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:
solution:
**Given:**

Pipe P fills (3)/(8) of the tank in 21 hours.

Pipe Q fills (2)/(7) of the tank in 16 hours.

P and Q run together for 2 hours.

Pipe R empties the tank in 3 hours.

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Work / Time

Total time = Total work / Combined efficiency

**Calculation:**

⇒ Time by P = dfrac{21 times 8}{3} = 56 hours

⇒ Time by Q = dfrac{16 times 7}{2} = 56 hours

⇒ P's efficiency = dfrac{1}{56} 

⇒ Q's efficiency = dfrac{1}{56} 

⇒ Total in 2 hours = 2 times ( dfrac{1}{56} + dfrac{1}{56} ) 

⇒ = 2 times dfrac{2}{56} = dfrac{4}{56} = dfrac{1}{14} 

R empties (1)/(14) of tank in 3 hours.

⇒ R’s efficiency = - dfrac{1/14}{3} = -dfrac{1}{42} 

⇒ Combined = dfrac{1}{56} + dfrac{1}{56} - dfrac{1}{42} 

Take LCM = 168

⇒ dfrac{3}{168} + dfrac{3}{168} - dfrac{4}{168} = dfrac{2}{168} = dfrac{1}{84} 

⇒ Time = dfrac{1}{1/84} = 84 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 84 hours.**
